items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: This guy was playing piano with Les Hyte's band, and I was trying to remember the trombone player -- Sonny Gravin was the trombone player.

ctx.x: alto; Marvin Johnson was playing third alto; that's when they were just using three saxaphones, and the tenor player was Chuck someone -- you know, I don't know, or remember him, but I do remember ... oh yeah, Henry Prince? Yeah, Henry Prince was the pianist, which was the bass player that was with Nat at first ... his name was Prince, Wesley Prince. Wesley Prince's brother.

This guy was playing piano with Les Hyte's band, and I was trying to remember the trombone player -- Sonny Gravin was the trombone player. See, the reason they're kind of rough is because in later years I got to know them better, you know, when I finally was accepted, and then I knew them better. But I was just trying to run down -- oh, and the bass player -- I don't know the bass player with Les's band, but that night, all the younger musicians thought that Buck Clayton's band cut Les Hyte's band, you know, but…

But anyway, it seems that Buck Clayton took his band to China. He got a job in Shanghai, China. The guys went to China, and they were stranded in China, the way I remember the story. Anyway, so I don't know whether the union or the musicians got together and didn't have a chance to send for them or what, but they were stranded over there.
